goal: A skill edit can be checked against a hard rule with one command: the runner starts a hermetic claude -p run of a case against a skill repo, as many times as asked, and the judge gives each run a verdict with its cost (M3 unit 1, Feature PR 2 of 5).
changed: python -m harness_lab run CASE --skill-root PATH [--runs N] [--model] [--budget-usd] [--timeout] [--keep DIR]. Each run gets a new temporary folder: the fixture as a one-commit git repo with no remote (any .git in the fixture is dropped), and the plugin and its plugin.json dependencies under plugins/<name>, so no path names the variant under test.

claude -p runs with project settings only, no MCP servers, only those plugins, no saved session, the case's tools and deny rules, a budget cap, and only PATH, HOME, USER, LOGNAME, TMPDIR and LANG from the caller's environment. A non-zero exit, a timeout or an unreadable stream makes the run UNJUDGEABLE; so does anything the judge already treats that way.
after commands get CASE_DIR, the folder of the case file, so a check script lives beside the case and not in the fixture the agent can change.

Each run prints its verdict, assertions, cost, tokens (input, output and cache writes), wall time and load average; the exit code is 1 if any run failed, else 2 if any was unjudgeable, else 0. The folder is deleted unless --keep copies it.
The note's guess that the built-in cc-plugin-* plugins came from the desktop environment is corrected: they load under env -i too.

claims.claim: On the receipt.py case, the runner gives PASS on both runs against agent-kit main and FAIL on both runs against a copy with the rule removed, at about $0.18 a run and 19 to 33 s on a machine at a load average of 3 to 4.
claims.check: python -m harness_lab run receipt/case.json --skill-root kit --runs 2, and the same with kit-norule

claims.claim: The runs were hermetic in the ways the README says: no stream mentions the variant's name, bstack and principles loaded in each, and each ran in its own temporary folder.
claims.check: grep and a script over the four kept streams' init events

claims.claim: Against a fake claude, the runner passes only the listed variables, names no variant in any path, stages one commit with no fixture .git, loads dependencies, refuses a missing dependency before starting claude, and turns a non-zero exit, a timeout or an unloaded dependency into UNJUDGEABLE.
claims.check: python -m unittest tests.test_harness_lab_runner (12 tests) and the full suite (359 tests, OK) on Python 3.12
